doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: T.V. All-Stars and Christmas album
summary: Albums by Tommy's writing, including a Christmas album with five singers made by alternating ensembles.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Well the only recording I really do now is just my own, or like some friend of mine tells me to call Tommy, call him, of course I’ll do that. We did two or three albums that Tommy wrote, called the T.V. All-Stars or something like that.
Yes, it was an unassuming title, you know, “T.V. All-Stars.”
Well they’d already used the World’s Greatest Jazz Band, so—
And then we also did, for these same people, a Christmas album that was kind of interesting. There was five different singers — Vic Damone, Jack Jones, Joe Williams, Diane Carroll and Patti Page.
Well I saw it in my drawer the other day. Annie was cleaning out the drawer the other day and that record was in there.

Yeah that sold a lot of records I think. We did that one with mirrors kind of. Because we had a rhythm section on every date, and then one date we used a string quartet, one day we used three French horns, one we used three trombones and a horn, and one of them we had a trumpet, trombone, sax. So what happens if you play them and you mix them all around, you can’t tell how many pieces is in there. You know what I mean?
Every track has a different combination on it. Alternating. It’s kind of like a shell game.
And the music becomes in the hands of some producer and you hope they do well with it.

Yeah. Well, it was a kind of a quickie, like two track direct digital, so you can rebalance the tracks but you can’t bring anything out, you know what I mean? You can raise a level of a track but that’s about it. And you can splice. And that’s it. But you can’t take mistakes out or put notes in that you wish were there. Like the fancy methods. Those things, they were fun, but you know I don’t know how long you could get away with that, trying to make a little group sound big.
